title: A robot on a gym floor: speed, position and distance

stimulus.title: A robot moving on a gym floor
stimulus.text: A robot moves on a flat gym floor, set up as the $xy$-plane with distances in meters. For $0 \le t \le 5$ seconds, its velocity components are given below, and at $t = 0$ the robot is at the point $(1, 2)$. A graphing calculator is required.

table.caption: Velocity components of the robot, in meters per second, and its position at $t = 0$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the speed of the robot at time $t = 4$. Find the acceleration vector of the robot at time $t = 4$.

accept: the square root of the sum of the squared velocity components at t = 4, evaluated to 1.032
both components from the calculator's numerical derivative, correct to three decimal places

parts.sample: Speed $= \sqrt{(4\sin 2.8 - 1)^2 + (2\cos 2.4 + 0.5)^2} \approx 1.032$ meters per second. Acceleration: $\mathbf{a}(4) = \left\langle x''(4), y''(4) \right\rangle = \left\langle 2.8\cos 2.8, -1.2\sin 2.4 \right\rangle \approx \left\langle -2.638, -0.811 \right\rangle$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find all times $t$, for $0 < t < 5$, at which the speed of the robot is 3 meters per second.

accept: speed = 3 written with the velocity components

parts.sample: Speed is 3 when $\sqrt{(4\sin(0.7t) - 1)^2 + (2\cos(0.6t) + 0.5)^2} = 3$. Solving on the calculator gives $t \approx 1.462$ and $t \approx 2.507$ seconds.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the position of the robot at time $t = 5$.

rubric.point: Uses the initial position with an integral of each velocity component: $x(5) = 1 + \int_0^5 x'(t)\,dt$ or $y(5) = 2 + \int_0^5 y'(t)\,dt$.
accept: initial value added to a definite integral from 0 to 5 of the velocity component, with dt

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the total distance traveled by the robot over the time interval $0 \le t \le 5$.

accept: the definite integral from 0 to 5 of the square root of the sum of the squared velocity components
